arguments.value: Phoenix Satellite TV licensed Beijing Tianying Jiuzhou Network Technology to use specified Phoenix program content for its online and related business, only under Phoenix’s rules. The license covered listed shows in an exhibit, with the scope updated yearly, and fees set under a related agreement. Beijing Tianying had no ownership in the content, had to keep Phoenix’s confidential information secure, could not sublicense or use the content outside the agreed business without written permission, and had to help protect Phoenix’s intellectual property. The agreement lasted five years, could be extended by Phoenix, could be terminated for breach, bankruptcy, illegality, or force majeure, and disputes would first be negotiated and then arbitrated in Hong Kong under PRC law.
